constraints.evidence: Slide 8: peak cash A $1.9M vs B $20.8M against the $18M cap; slide 12 runs A's peak through ten stress cases (max $7.2M); B at 2.6 units/door is $26.4M (slide 9).
Payback is built into the headline: A +$2.4M at 25% ACoS, +$0.4M at 28%, -$2.3M at 32%; breakeven ACoS 28.6% (slide 11). B never pays back; J pays back in 2029.
Group margin is computed year by year (slides 8, 17, 18): A min 9.5%, B 4.5%/6.6%/7.5% for 2027-29, with the formula (15.4 − 8.7) ÷ (140 + 11.3) = 4.5%.
Option J is compared directly as the forgone alternative (slides 6, 8, Alternatives): +$1.8M cash, peak $1.1M, $7M revenue; one launch in 2027 is stated as a board limit.

Slide 10 and the recommendation say no route reaches $40M by 2030 within the cash limits (A ~$26M, B $37.6M but breaches limits). The board is asked to restate the ambition as '$25M+ by 2030, on a path to $40M by ~2032'.
Slides 3, 9 and 14: the 4.0 delisting line, 2.6 median at 4% awareness, 3.5 in the 10-20% band, and the CEO's 15% trigger rejected in favour of ≥20% plus a door test.
Slide 7 builds the full per-unit stack: Amazon $4.73 at 25% ACoS, $4.01 at 28%, $3.05 at 32%; retail $7.55 with co-op and returns. These feed the cash model on slides 17-18.
Slides 17-18 use A at $2.1M a year plus $0.8M setup, and B at $9.6M a year plus $1.96M of 2027 one-offs and later fixtures. Slide 7 shows retail would need ~4,250 doors to cover its fixed cost.
Inventory is four months of landed cost ($4.575 per unit) and is deducted from cash on slide 17 (-0.46/-0.40/-0.44/-0.38). It is stated as an assumption and its effect is discussed on slide 19.

Slides 11 and 12: the plan's 25% is challenged against the pilot's 28% and the 32% median (range 26-38%), noting that ad cost per click rises. A's revenue of $7-26M sits in the benchmark band, and the headline states the 28.6% breakeven.

Slides 11, 12, 15: duty at 25% costs -$0.35 per unit and -$1.1M by 2030, and breakeven falls from 28.6% to 27.0%. The tariff decision is a signpost, and Gate 1 lowers each ACoS threshold by ~1.5 pts if duty rises.
Slides 5 and 13: the Korean-only label complaint (6%) is fixed by US labelling, MoCRA registration and safety substantiation in Stage 1. The $0.8M setup and $0.5M a year are in the cash numbers.

29% repeat is set against the 31% benchmark and Korea's 48% (slides 5, 13, 15). Repeat is tracked at Gate 1, and volume is stress-tested (70%/85%/115% grid; a 4% cushion at 28% ACoS). 300k units is explicitly flagged as assuming new SKUs sell like the first three.

alternatives.evidence: Option B is tested on all three board limits (slides 8, 9, 18): -$20.8M peak, no payback, 4.5% margin in 2027. The 4.5 units/door input is shown to match the >20% awareness band, and the 1.3× halo is shown to be a correlation. B would need a 3.1× halo or 23.5 units/door to pay back, and Mooncrest is used as the precedent.

Slide 14 proposes a 12-month limited-door test at ≥4.0 units/door/week, with the cost base 're-sized to the test', but only after ≥20% awareness (Gate 2, 2029). It is not tested as a 2027 option: no scaled-down marketing or field-team cost is priced, and there is no check of whether a test erases A's thin payback margin. The only reason given for not doing it now is that awareness is 4%, so sell-through would be ~2.6.

Option J is modelled with numbers on slides 6 and 8 (+$1.8M cash, $1.1M peak, 10.1% min margin, payback 2029) and compared with A. The document explains why A is preferred (US growth of 17% vs 1.5%, 4× revenue, the ambition) and works out the crossover at ACoS of about 26%. The red gate frees the 2028 slot for Japan. Deferral past the tariff decision and a keep-the-cross-border-listing option are not discussed.

No leaner-fixed-cost variant of Option A is evaluated. The $2.1M a year base is taken as given; the amber gate only 'freezes new fixed cost'. The trade-off of trimming brand marketing against payback is not explored.

sensitivities.evidence: The cash-by-ACoS grid (25-38%) and the stress table show +$2.4M at 25%, +$0.4M at 28% and -$2.3M at 32%. The 28.6% breakeven is derived (each +1 pt = -$0.67M), falling to 27.0% with the tariff. The cap and margin floor are shown to hold (peak ≤$7.2M, margin ≥8.8%), and the Gate 1 ACoS thresholds say what to do if the gate is missed.

Slide 9 and 14: 2.6 units/door at 4% awareness and 3.5 at 10-20% against the 4.0 line, with only >20% clearing it (4.6). B's peak is $20.8M at 4.5 and $26.4M at 2.6 with no halo. B needs 23.5 units/door or a 3.1× halo to pay back, and the retail trigger is raised to 20%.

Slide 11 grid at 70/85/100/115% volume. Payback survives a 21% shortfall at 25% ACoS and only 4% at 28%. The Gaon Lab/Yeoreum stall case gives -$7.1M. 300k units is sense-checked against the pilot run-rate (168k a year), and Gate 1 sets 70% of plan as the red threshold. The $5.2B trade-press figure is rejected, and Saebom is set against the two stalled brands.

overclaim.quote: Amazon-led (A) is the only route that fits the board's limits (also the governing thought: "it is the only route within the board's limits")

omissions: The document's own evidence-based central case (32% median ACoS) misses the board's payback limit, and the ask is for the board to pre-agree a payback slip to ~2031-32. Yet the headline says A is within the limits. Slide 8 also shows J passing all three limits, which contradicts 'only route'.

No priced version of the limited-door retail test and no leaner Option A fixed-cost variant. A deck should show what the test costs, and whether it or a lower fixed-cost base would protect A's payback margin.

No plan or cost for moving aided awareness from 4% to the ≥20% trigger, even though the document calls this 'the real retail question'. The cash and time needed to reach 20% are not estimated, so the retail option has no evidenced route to being exercised.
No explicit statement of what happens to the existing cross-border Amazon listing, or of the transition from the cross-border seller to Onsoo's own US entity.
unsupported_assumptions: "about $40M by 2032 if it keeps growing ~29% a year": holds the 2029→30 growth rate for two more years, although the plan's own growth is decelerating (86%, 52%, 29%) and the document argues ad costs rise at scale.

"Waiting a year would not resolve the key unknown, ad cost at scale, which can only be learned by scaling in the US": asserted with no evidence. It is used to dismiss the alternative of waiting a year, and the existing cross-border listing could keep generating data.

"awareness is cheaper to build with the off-Amazon social budget than with $6M of in-store marketing": no cost-per-awareness-point evidence in the pack. The $0.7M a year social budget is assumed to be enough to take awareness from 4% to ≥20%.

"Most likely outcome: removal after the 12-month review": rests on the median of a 46-brand retail-analytics sample applied to Onsoo's awareness band. It is stated as a likely outcome without a probability.
